subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment options & HIPAA/SOC2 requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Deployment options & HIPAA/SOC2 requirements

Hi Sarah 

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps while we align internally:

Summary of needs you shared:
- Elara will be processing PHI and requires HIPAA coverage (BAA).
- SOC2 Type II evidence required for our security team and auditors.
- Data residency: US only.
- Audit logs / exportable access logs for compliance and quarterly audits.
- Key management (KMS/HSM) and customer-managed keys are preferred.
- Preference toward Private VPC/on-prem, but open to Dedicated if SLAs and BAA align.

Initial guidance from Redwood:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started; recommended for non-PHI or pilot (we can discuss limited-Baa options, but shared tenancy has constraints for PHI).
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation 

  - compatible with BAA and most enterprise security needs.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full isolation, customer-managed networking and KMS 

  - best for regulated workflows and audits.

Attachments I'm sharing now: Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_report_2025.pdf (SOC2 report) and a draft BAA (BAA_Draft_Elara.pdf). I'm also attaching a short deployment-options overview.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm your procurement timeline and decision criteria (e.g., must be Private, or Dedicated acceptable)?
2) Please share any specific questionnaire items we should prioritize for the tech deep-dive (you mentioned retention / log export).
3) Would Tue/Wed next week work for a technical call with Dylan & Rishi to walk architecture and timelines?

Happy to adjust based on your security team's preferences 

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Marissa 

Appreciate the quick recap and the documents. I uploaded the Elara security questionnaire for your team (see attachment). A few clarifying notes from our side:
- Procurement is leaning toward Private VPC for PHI if timelines and costs are reasonable. Dedicated is a potential second choice if it meets BAA and provides the necessary audit logs/export.
- We need retention policies documented (how long logs are kept, ability to export on demand).
- Our auditors will ask for: SOC2 Type II report, list of subservice providers, encryption at rest details (KMS), access control policies, and sample audit logs (last 90 days).
- Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated or Private? Is HSM available for on-prem?
- Timeline: procurement kickoff targeted for first week of August; vendor selection expected mid-August.

I attached the questionnaire and put procurement on cc (procurement@elara-health.com). If you can get answers to the auditor items and timeline estimates before our tech call, that would help speed procurement.

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment options & HIPAA/SOC2 requirements

Hi Sarah 

Thanks 

This is helpful. Answers and proposed timelines below (high-level; we'll review in the tech deep-dive):

Key compliance items:
- SOC2 Type II: attached is our 2025 report (Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_report_2025.pdf). We can provide the standard SOC2 package, list of subservice providers, and control narratives.
- BAA: we attached a BAA draft (BAA_Draft_Elara.pdf). We're happy to take your redlines; legal typically turns around straightforward redlines in 3-5 business days.
- Audit logs / retention: Redwood can export access logs and audit trails on demand. Default retention for audit logs in Dedicated is 12 months; Private deployments can be configured per customer policy. We can provide a sample log export for the last 90 days ahead of the call.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed KMS is supported in Private VPC and Dedicated (via BYOK integration). On-prem deployments can use HSM integrations as required.

Deployment modes (trade-offs):
- Hosted API:
  - Pros: fastest, no infra work, lower cost for pilots.
  - Cons: shared tenancy; not recommended for PHI at scale. BAA possible for some enterprise customers but with strict controls; discuss if you need this for a pilot only.
- Dedicated capacity:
  - Pros: tenant isolation, predictable throughput, compatible with BAA, supports BYOK KMS, faster provisioning than full Private.
  - Cons: reserved capacity costs, config window for provisioning (2-4 weeks to provision and test).
- Private VPC / On-prem:
  - Pros: full isolation, customer-managed networking and keys, best for audits and strict compliance.
  - Cons: longer lead time (6-10 weeks), higher setup effort.

Estimated timelines (ballpark):
- SOC2 evidence & sample logs: 3 business days to gather and deliver sample export.
- Dedicated provisioning & validation: ~2-4 weeks from contract.
- Private VPC (cloud-hosted) or on-prem: ~6-10 weeks from scoping and contract.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Dylan + Rishi (45-60m) to go through questionnaire and audit evidence. Proposed windows: Tue Jul 21 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed Jul 22 13:00-14:00 PT.
2) I'll route SOC2 artifacts and a sample audit log export before the call.
3) If procurement wants to start BAA redlines now, send them and I'll loop legal.

Would either of those windows work?

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: deployment-options-overview.pdf (pdf, 180KB)
